verses: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
“Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
Going on a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat, mending their nets.
Immediately Jesus called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him.
Then Jesus and His companions went to Capernaum, and right away Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and began to teach.
The people were astonished at His teaching, because He taught as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.
Suddenly a man with an unclean spirit cried out in the synagogue:
“What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”
But Jesus rebuked the spirit. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!”
At this, the unclean spirit threw the man into convulsions and came out with a loud shriek.
All the people were amazed and began to ask one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!”
And the news about Jesus spread quickly through the whole region of Galilee.
As soon as Jesus and His companions had left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
Simon’s mother-in-law was sick in bed with a fever, and they promptly told Jesus about her.
So He went to her, took her by the hand, and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began to serve them.
That evening, after sunset, people brought to Jesus all the sick and demon-possessed,
and the whole town gathered at the door.
And He healed many who were ill with various diseases and drove out many demons. But He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew who He was.
Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and went out to a solitary place to pray.
Simon and his companions went to look for Him,
and when they found Him, they said, “Everyone is looking for You!”
But Jesus answered, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns so I can preach there as well, for that is why I have come.”
So He went throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons.
title: A Day with Jesus
season_line: Jesus has just announced that God's kingdom is near, and now we watch one full day of what that looks like in a small fishing town.
big_idea: Jesus has authority over everything, yet He lets the Father, not the crowd, set the pace of His days.
frame: Most of us live like the disciples at the end of this reading, sure that everyone needs us and that the loudest demand must be answered first. Jesus had more power and more need around Him than anyone. Still, He got up in the dark to be alone with His Father, and from there He knew what the day was for. Rest and prayer were not a break from His mission. They were how He stayed on it. That rhythm goes back to God resting on the seventh day ({{Genesis 2:2-3|Genesis 2:2–3}}), and Jesus later invites His tired followers to come away with Him ({{Mark 6:31|Mark 6:31}}). Carry this posture today: let His voice, not your inbox, decide what matters most.

carry.text: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and went out to a solitary place to pray.

glance.head: Called from the nets
glance.line: Jesus calls four fishermen, and they leave their work and family business to follow Him.

glance.head: Authority in the synagogue
glance.line: Jesus teaches with His own authority and silences an unclean spirit with a word.

glance.head: Healing at the door
glance.line: He heals Simon's mother-in-law, and by evening the whole town crowds His door.

glance.head: Prayer before the crowds
glance.line: Jesus rises early to pray, then moves on to preach in other towns instead of staying where He's wanted.

understand: Yesterday Jesus announced that the time had come and God's kingdom was near. Today Mark shows us what that means in real life. Mark loves the word 'immediately.' His story moves fast, and in one day in Capernaum, a fishing town on the Sea of Galilee, we see Jesus call, teach, cast out evil, and heal.

In those days, students chose a rabbi to follow. Here the rabbi chooses them, and He picks working fishermen, not scholars. The scribes taught by quoting earlier teachers. Jesus speaks on His own authority, and even evil spirits obey Him. The spirit calls Him the Holy One of God, but Jesus silences it. He will make Himself known on His own terms, and most fully at the cross ({{Mark 15:39|Mark 15:39}}).

The details matter. Sabbath ended at sunset, which is why the crowds waited until evening to carry their sick to Him. Simon's mother-in-law gets up and serves, the same kind of service Jesus says He came to give ({{Mark 10:45|Mark 10:45}}). Then, with the whole town looking for Him, Jesus slips away to pray. Prayer is where He hears His purpose again: go on to the next towns, for that is why I have come.

word.gloss: The Greek word means the right and the power to act, authority that belongs to someone rather than being borrowed. Jesus did not cite other teachers. He spoke, and teaching, spirits, and sickness answered to Him.

god.short: Before your phone, take five quiet minutes and ask: Lord, what is today for?
god.full: Before you check your phone or messages, sit quietly for five minutes. Ask God plainly, 'What is today for?' and listen before the demands start.
god.why: Jesus regularly withdrew to quiet places to pray ({{Luke 5:16|Luke 5:16}}).

together.short: Each name one thing you'll let go of today.
together.full: Over coffee, each of you name one thing you won't let crowd out what matters today. Then say, 'Go for it,' to each other.

others.short: Give one person your full, unhurried attention today, phone away.
others.full: Jesus went to a sick woman and took her by the hand. Today, with one person, maybe a child, a coworker, or a tired friend, put your phone away and give them your full attention.
others.why: Jesus stopped for people the crowd overlooked ({{Mark 5:30-34|Mark 5:30–34}}).

tonight: Whose expectations set the pace of our day today, and what would it look like to let Jesus set it tomorrow?
